subtopic: Handling a legal or tax notice
subtype: Approach: revising record-keeping after the episode [Revision]
passage:
Coach's note, Sunday. Noor writing about Imran, who came to our community finance desk after a difficult tax matter.
The matter had been settled, but Imran's records had been a mess: small freelance payments in phone messages, receipts in a shoebox. Since then, Imran has changed how things work. On the first Sunday of each month, Imran turns up with a sealed envelope of receipts and screenshots and enters each one in a plain sheet with a column for side income.
I did not tell Imran what to record; I only asked what next year's filing would need. Imran said, "Fewer mismatches, and no scramble." Today the sheet matched the bank statement line by line, and Imran's shoulders eased.
— Noor

qa.q: On which day of the month does Imran bring the envelope?
qa.a: Imran brings it on the first Sunday of each month.

qa.q: What was Imran probably feeling when the sheet matched the bank statement?
qa.a: Imran was probably relieved and a bit proud, shown by the shoulders easing after a messy year.

qa.q: What could Imran do if a payment has no receipt?
qa.a: Imran could write it in the sheet the same day with the date, amount and payer, and ask the payer for a note if possible.

qa.q: What is it like for Noor to watch Imran's new routine?
qa.a: Noor is encouraged and glad, seeing the routine grow by Imran's own choice and only asking questions about it.

grounding: The note shows a person, after settling a tax matter, tracking side income and receipts monthly so that the next filing has complete records.
